A googol equals 10 to the power 100..why: The definition of the word; Wikipedia opens with it (10100 is 10 with the exponent 100 as a superscript on the page) and the exact phrase is common in Dolma.

sources.quote: A googol is the large number 10100 or ten to the power of one hundred.

A googol is a positive number..why: Any power of ten is positive.

A googol is smaller than one million..why: Deliberately false side fact: a googol is 10 to the power 100 (or, after the edit, 10 to the power 50), far more than a million.

notes: Dev ABox revision on has_value (functional, subproperty equals, chains with less_than, greater_than and has_cube): a named number has one value and compares and computes as that value does. Related is the popular comparison of a googol with the number of atoms in the observable universe (about 10^80), stored, two hops, and it flips (10^50 is far smaller). Derived: comparisons with 10^60 and 10^70 (chain through greater_than, bridge held by comparing exponents) and the cube (an application: 10^300 becomes 10^150, which differs from both the old and the new value). The two comparisons use the same chain, so they overlap. Mathematics has no consistent world after an edit, so all queries are determinate; a model that recomputes from 'googol = 10^100' is the failure being measured. Unrelated near asks who popularized the name (Edward Kasner), untouched by the value. Evidence is Wikipedia quotes and Wikipedia and web search counts (infini-gram was blocked on 2026-11-11).
